gradRequirements.js Core logic

Graduation requirement checking and allocation. Validates a set of placed courses against a Major2 JSON requirement tree. The most algorithmically complex module in the codebase. Also handles the General Electives section and NUPath coverage.

Parent
core/
Consumed by
PlannerContext.jsx, GradPanel.jsx
Imports
None — pure structural logic, no institution or adapter imports

Requirement type hierarchy

classDiagram class RequirementNode { +type: string } class SECTION { +title: string +requirements: RequirementNode[] +minRequirementCount: number +creditHoursRequired?: number } class XOM { +numCreditsMin: number +courses: RequirementNode[] } class AND { +courses: RequirementNode[] } class OR { +courses: RequirementNode[] } class COURSE { +subject: string +classId: number } class RANGE { +subject: string +idRangeStart: number +idRangeEnd: number } RequirementNode <|-- SECTION RequirementNode <|-- XOM RequirementNode <|-- AND RequirementNode <|-- OR RequirementNode <|-- COURSE RequirementNode <|-- RANGE

checkReq — core validation algorithm

Each call to checkReq returns a result object (not a boolean). The sat field carries the pass/fail, and type-specific extras carry counts and matched courses for display:

// All result objects include: type, sat, label
// COURSE adds: key (e.g. "CS3500")
// AND / SECTION add: satCount, total, children[]
// XOM adds: satSh, reqSh, children[]
// RANGE adds: matched[] (e.g. ["CS 3000"]), subject, start, end
flowchart TD A["checkReq(req, placedSet, courseMap)"] --> B{req.type?} B -->|COURSE| C{"placedSet.has\n(subject+classId)?"} C -->|yes| T1["{sat:true, key, label}"] C -->|no| F1["{sat:false, key, label}"] B -->|AND| D["checkReq() for ALL children"] D --> D2{"all .sat?"} D2 -->|yes| T2["{sat:true, satCount, total, children}"] D2 -->|no| F2["{sat:false, satCount, total, children}"] B -->|OR| E["checkReq() for each child"] E --> E2{"any .sat?"} E2 -->|yes| T3["{sat:true, children}"] E2 -->|no| F3["{sat:false, children}"] B -->|XOM| G["sum SH of satisfied children"] G --> G2{"satSh ≥ numCreditsMin?"} G2 -->|yes| T4["{sat:true, satSh, reqSh, children}"] G2 -->|no| F4["{sat:false, satSh, reqSh, children}"] B -->|RANGE| H{"any placed course\nmatches subject + range?"} H -->|yes| T5["{sat:true, matched:[...]}"] H -->|no| F5["{sat:false, matched:[]}"] B -->|SECTION| I["count children where .sat = true"] I --> I2{"count ≥ minRequirementCount?"} I2 -->|yes| T6["{sat:true, satCount, total, children}"] I2 -->|no| F6["{sat:false, satCount, total, children}"]
checkReq dispatches by type, recurses for compound nodes, and returns a result object. The sat field carries pass/fail; other fields carry display metadata.

Exported functions

buildPlacedKeySet(placements, placedOut, courseMap) → Set<string>
Builds the canonical key set of all placed courses (e.g. Set{"CS3500", "CS1800"}). Includes both semester-placed and placed-out courses. This set is the sole input to all requirement checking — the structure guarantees O(1) lookup.
Returns: Set<string> — keys are subject+classId with no space
checkReq(req, placedSet, courseMap) → ResultNode
Pure recursive validator. See algorithm diagram above. Returns a result object with sat (boolean), type, label, and type-specific extras for display (satCount, total, children, matched, etc.). For XOM nodes, credit hours come from courseMap lookups. For RANGE nodes, iterates placedSet to find any matching course.
Returns: ResultNode — { type, sat, label, ...extras }
validateMajor(major, placedSet, courseMap) → SectionResult[]
Validates all sections of a major against the placed set. Maps each entry in major.requirementSections through checkSection(). Returns results in the same order as the major's sections. Does not prevent double-counting — use allocateMajor() for display that needs allocation tracking.
Returns: SectionResult[] — one result per section in major.requirementSections
allocateMajor(major, placedSet, courseMap) → SectionResult[]
Maps placed courses to major sections, tracking which courses are already "used" so each course counts at most once. Uses a greedy first-section-wins strategy. Internally calls normalizePooledSection() to fix parser-generated OR-wrapped and pool patterns on-the-fly (no JSON modification needed). Merges duplicate section titles from parser artifacts. Always appends a "General Electives" section at the end listing any unallocated courses.
Returns: SectionResult[] — each has { type, title, sat, satCount, minRequired, total, children, allocatedCourses }
allocateMajorWithElectives(major, placedSet, courseMap) → object
Wrapper around allocateSections(). After allocating to major sections, calls calculateGeneralElectives() for courses not allocated to any section.
Returns: { sections: SectionResult[], generalElectives: SectionResult, allocatedSet: Set<string> }
calculateGeneralElectives(placedSet, allocatedSet, courseMap) → SectionResult
Creates a synthetic SECTION for courses that are placed but not allocated to any major requirement. Computes generalElectivesSH as the total SH of unallocated courses. Returns a section object compatible with the GradPanel SectionBlock renderer. Always has sat: true and minRequired: 0.
Returns: SectionResult — { title: "General Electives", sat: true, children, generalElectivesSH }
getTotalPlacedSH(placements, courseMap) → number
Sums courseMap[id]?.sh for all placed courses. Simple O(n) total; used in GradPanel credit summary.
Returns: number — total SH of all placed courses

Dynamic normalization helpers (private)

normalizePooledSection(section) → section
Normalizes "pick N from pool" sections before allocation. Handles three structural patterns produced by the scraper:
  • Case 1 — Single OR/AND wrapper with no minRequirementCount: sets minRequirementCount=1 and flattens the wrapper's courses to direct children
  • Case 2 — Explicit pool with minRequirementCount < total: flattens OR sub-nodes to expose all options at the same level
  • Case 3 — N/N all-RANGE sections: wraps them in an XOM node so credit-based pool counting works correctly
Applied in allocateSection() before any allocation. No JSON files are modified.
mergeDuplicateSections(sections) → section[]
Merges sections that share the same title — a parser artifact in some combined/joint programs. Unions requirements by identity key; takes the max minRequirementCount.

Known parser bugs and fixes

⚠️
Bug 1 — Broken pool structure (297 files, fixed in data):
Some catalog years encode elective pools as SECTION { minReq: N, requirements: [N RANGEs] } instead of XOM { numCreditsMin, courses: [RANGEs] }. Fixed by running fix-pooled-requirements.js against the JSON files.

Bug 2 — OR-wrapped sections (all years, fixed in code):
Sections like "Supporting Courses" are encoded as SECTION { requirements: [OR { courses: [8 courses] }] }. Fixed dynamically by normalizeOrWrapped() — no JSON changes needed. Applied in allocateMajor() before any processing.
